programming_tips.topic: SGI.5 (Super Geometric Intelligence) Activation and Tolerance Setting
programming_tips.code_example:
M130 (enable SGI.5)
#8500 = 0.005 (set SGI tolerance to 5um)
G01 X... Y... Z... F5000
(machining moves)
M131 (disable SGI.5)
programming_tips.description: SGI.5 is Makino's proprietary smoothing technology that dynamically adjusts feed rate and path interpolation for optimal surface finish. Activate with M130, deactivate with M131. The tolerance is set via system variable #8500 (in mm). Typical values: 0.002-0.005mm for finishing, 0.01-0.02mm for roughing. SGI.5 produces superior surface finish on complex 3D surfaces compared to standard G05.1 AICC.
gotchas: SGI.5 tolerance in #8500 is in mm — setting 0.05 instead of 0.005 produces visibly scalloped surfaces
SGI.5 slows feed rate in tight-radius areas — cycle time may increase 10-15% vs raw path
Cannot use SGI.5 with G41/G42 cutter compensation active
SGI.5 is most effective on 3D contouring — minimal benefit on 2D pocket milling

programming_tips.topic: ADC (Active Damping Control) for Deep Pocket Chatter Suppression
programming_tips.code_example:
M140 (enable ADC)
G01 Z-150.0 F200 (deep pocket entry)
(pocket milling moves with long tool)
M141 (disable ADC when done)
programming_tips.description: ADC detects chatter vibration in real time and modulates spindle speed and feed to suppress resonance. Extremely effective for deep pocket milling with long tool extensions (>5xD). ADC works alongside SGI.5 — both can be active simultaneously. The system variable #8600 controls ADC sensitivity (0-100, default 50).
gotchas: ADC introduces minor RPM fluctuations visible on the spindle load meter — this is normal operation
ADC is not a substitute for proper tool selection — always minimize tool extension first
ADC effectiveness diminishes above 12,000 RPM due to sensor bandwidth
Monitor surface finish on first part when ADC is active — rarely, ADC can produce slight witness marks at damping frequency shifts

source.handbook_title: Makino a51nx Horizontal Machining Center Operator's Manual

programming_tips.code_example:
M88 (TSC on — 70 bar through spindle)
G83 Z-80.0 R2.0 Q10.0 F250 (deep drill with TSC)
M89 (TSC off)
M08 (switch to flood for face milling)
programming_tips.description: The a51nx TSC system delivers 70 bar (1015 psi) coolant through the spindle and tool. Essential for: deep hole drilling (>3xD), tapping in stainless/titanium, and chip evacuation in horizontal machining where gravity works against you. Use TSC-compatible HSK-A63 holders with through-coolant paths. Always activate TSC before starting the cut — pressurization takes ~0.5 sec.
gotchas: TSC requires through-coolant tool holders — standard collet chucks block the coolant path
Never run TSC with an empty coolant tank — destroys the high-pressure pump within minutes
TSC at 70 bar creates significant spray — ensure enclosure seals are intact
For tapping with TSC, reduce pressure to 35 bar via parameter to avoid breaking small taps (<M6)

source.handbook_title: Makino a51nx Horizontal Machining Center Operator's Manual

programming_tips.code_example:
G28 G91 Z0 (home Z)
G28 G91 X0 Y0 (home XY)
G91 G28 B0 (home B-axis)
M50 (execute pallet change — 6.9 sec)
G54 (activate WCS for new pallet)
(begin machining on fresh pallet)
programming_tips.description: The a51nx 2-pallet APC enables loading one pallet while machining the other. Key rules: always home all axes before M50 pallet change. Each pallet should have independent work offsets (e.g., Pallet 1 = G54, Pallet 2 = G55). Use the Pro6 pallet management screen to assign programs per pallet for fully automatic production. Pallet change time is 6.9 seconds.
gotchas: ALL axes must be at home position before M50 — any axis not homed causes PC5001 alarm
Work offsets must be set independently per pallet — never assume Pallet 2 matches Pallet 1
The B-axis MUST be at 0 or an indexed position before pallet change
Pallet cone surfaces must be clean — chip contamination causes repeatability errors up to 10um

source.handbook_title: Makino a51nx Horizontal Machining Center Operator's Manual

programming_tips.code_example:
(Face 1 — B0)
G54
B0 M10 (index B to 0, clamp)
(machining Face 1)
(Face 2 — B90)
G55
M11 (unclamp B)
B90. M10 (index to 90, clamp)
(machining Face 2)
(repeat for B180, B270)
programming_tips.description: Tombstone fixturing on the a51nx uses the B-axis to present 4 faces (B0, B90, B180, B270) of a tombstone fixture. Each face gets its own work offset (G54-G57 or G54.1 Pxx). Always clamp B-axis (M10) before cutting and unclamp (M11) before rotating. Use the Pro6 B-axis calibration routine to verify indexing accuracy at all 4 positions before production.
gotchas: Always unclamp (M11) before commanding B-axis rotation — rotating against clamp causes B-axis alarm
Tombstone weight affects B-axis indexing time — heavy tombstones may need reduced rapid rate
Tool length offset is measured from spindle face — verify TLO is correct for each B-axis position
Consider chip evacuation on each face — horizontal B90/B270 faces drain chips, B0 face traps them

programming_tips.topic: G68.2 Tilted Working Plane for 3+2 Machining
programming_tips.code_example:
G90 G00 G54
G68.2 X0 Y0 Z0 I30 J0 K0 (tilt 30 deg around X)
G43.4 H01 (activate TCPC)
G01 X10. Y10. Z-5. F500 (machine in tilted plane)
G69 (cancel tilted plane)
G49 (cancel TCPC)
programming_tips.description: G68.2 establishes a tilted (inclined) working plane defined by Euler angles I, J, K. Combined with G43.4 TCPC, this enables full 3+2 machining using the B-axis. The control transforms all subsequent X/Y/Z commands into the tilted coordinate system. Cancel with G69. Essential for machining angled features without dedicated 5-axis CAM.
gotchas: G68.2 MUST be paired with G43.4 (TCPC) — without TCPC, tool tip position is wrong in tilted plane
Cancel order matters: G69 first, then G49 — reversing causes position jump
Euler angle convention (I/J/K) follows Fanuc standard: I=rotation around X, J=around Y, K=around Z
Verify G68.2 setup with a test cut in foam/wax before committing to production material

programming_tips.topic: Makino System Variables #8xxx for Machine Monitoring
programming_tips.code_example:
#100 = #8500 (read current SGI tolerance)
#101 = #8600 (read ADC sensitivity)
#102 = #8700 (read spindle bearing temperature)
IF [#102 GT 55.0] THEN #3000=1 (SPINDLE TOO HOT)
programming_tips.description: Makino-specific system variables in the #8000-#8999 range provide access to machine-specific data: #8500=SGI tolerance, #8600=ADC sensitivity, #8700-#8710=spindle thermal data, #8800-#8810=axis load percentages. These enable adaptive machining macros that respond to real-time machine conditions.
gotchas: #8xxx variables are Makino-specific — programs using them will NOT run on other Fanuc machines
Some #8xxx variables are read-only — writing to read-only addresses generates PS alarm
Values update in real time but macro reads have ~10ms latency — not suitable for high-frequency control
Document all #8xxx usage in program header for portability awareness

programming_tips.topic: AI Nano Contour Control (G05.1 Q1) vs AICC (G05 P10000)
programming_tips.code_example:
G05.1 Q1 (preferred — AI Nano, newest algorithm)
(or)
G05 P10000 (legacy AICC — use for programs written for older Makino)
programming_tips.description: Pro6 supports two high-speed machining modes: G05.1 Q1 (AI Nano Contour Control — newer, preferred) and G05 P10000 (AICC — legacy). AI Nano provides smoother feed transitions and tighter tolerance tracking. Use AI Nano for all new programs. AICC compatibility is retained for running older programs without reposting. Both modes engage the 200-block lookahead buffer.
gotchas: Do not mix G05.1 Q1 and G05 P10000 in the same program — cancel one before activating the other
Both modes require G01/G02/G03 moves — G00 rapid moves bypass the smoothing buffer
AI Nano tolerance is affected by feed rate — reduce F for tighter tolerance at expense of cycle time
Cancel either mode before tool change or M30

programming_tips.topic: Safe Program Start Block (Makino HMC Standard)
programming_tips.code_example:
O0001 (PROGRAM NAME - PART-001)
G00 G17 G40 G49 G54 G80 G90
G28 G91 Z0 (home Z first)
G28 G91 X0 Y0 (home XY)
M11 (unclamp B)
G28 G91 B0 (home B-axis)
M10 (clamp B)
T01 M06 (first tool change)
programming_tips.description: Standard safe start for Makino HMC programs. Key additions vs VMC: B-axis must be homed and clamped before any cutting. Always home Z first to clear workpiece, then XY, then B. The B-axis unclamp/rotate/clamp sequence (M11/Bxx/M10) must be explicit — omitting M11 before B rotation causes B-axis damage alarm.
gotchas: NEVER omit G49 in safe start — residual TLO from previous program can cause Z crash
B-axis home MUST include M11 (unclamp) before and M10 (clamp) after
If running after pallet change, verify correct WCS is selected for the current pallet
Include G69 in safe start if any programs use G68.2 tilted working plane

source.handbook_title: Makino a51nx Horizontal Machining Center Operator's Manual

programming_tips.description: In horizontal machining, gravity assists chip evacuation — a major advantage over VMCs. However, chips can accumulate on B0 face (top of tombstone) and inside deep pockets. Strategies: (1) Use through-spindle coolant (M88) for all deep hole operations, (2) Program air blast (M300) between operations to clear chip buildup on fixture, (3) Orient pockets toward gravity (B90/B270) when possible, (4) Use chip-breaking peck cycles even for shallow holes to prevent bird-nesting.
gotchas: B0 face (top of tombstone) accumulates chips — program periodic M300 air blast to clear
Long horizontal bores at B90/B270 can trap chips at the bottom — use TSC + peck cycle
Aluminum chips tend to weld to HSK taper — clean taper frequently
Program chip conveyor activation (M-code varies) during long cycle times
